html:
Togo is a narrow country in West Africa, under 115 kilometres wide, running north from the Gulf of Guinea. Its capital is Lomé.

From the 1500s this stretch of shore was part of the Slave Coast, where Europeans bought captives for the Atlantic trade. Germany declared the protectorate of Togoland in 1884.

  • 1914: British and French troops took it in the first weeks of World War I.
  • 1916 to 1922: split. The west went to Britain and later joined the Gold Coast, now Ghana. The east, ruled by France, is today's Togo.
  • 1960: independence under Sylvanus Olympio, one of many states freed in the Year of Africa.
  • 1963: Olympio was killed in the first coup in independent sub-Saharan Africa.
  • 1967 to 2005: Gnassingbé Eyadéma ruled for 38 years.
  • 2005: his son Faure Gnassingbé took over and still rules.
sum: Togo is a narrow country in West Africa, under 115 kilometres wide, running north from the Gulf of Guinea. Its capital is Lomé.
